evidence.snippet: Vancomycin binds to the D-ala-D-ala terminus of the nascent peptidoglycan precursor lipid II, preventing cell wall biosynthesis.
evidence.explanation: Vancomycin directly binds the D-alanyl-D-alanine (D-ala-D-ala) terminus of peptidoglycan precursor lipid II, which is the molecular basis of its antibacterial mechanism.

evidence.snippet: They inhibit bacterial cell wall biosynthesis by binding to the D-Ala-D-Ala C-terminus of peptidoglycan precursors.
evidence.explanation: Glycopeptide antibiotics including vancomycin inhibit cell wall biosynthesis by binding to the D-Ala-D-Ala C-terminus of peptidoglycan precursors, directly confirming the binding relationship.

paper.title: New insights into glycopeptide antibiotic binding to cell wall precursors using SPR and NMR spectroscopy.

evidence.snippet: Vancomycin is a critical glycopeptide antibiotic for treating severe infections caused by Gram-positive bacteria, particularly MRSA and Clostridioides difficile, by inhibiting cell wall synthesis through binding to D-Ala-D-Ala termini of peptidoglycan precursors.
evidence.explanation: D-Ala-D-Ala termini of peptidoglycan precursors are the substrates whose accessibility is required for peptidoglycan biosynthesis; vancomycin's binding to them disrupts the process, confirming that D-alanyl-D-alanine participates in peptidoglycan biosynthetic process.
